title: QBR + Health Check — Acme Corp
summary: Quarterly business review focused on usage trends, cost drivers, recent reliability incidents and roadmap alignment. Customer is running production conversational features on Redwood Dedicated with occasional spikes. Top asks: clearer cost breakdown, SLA confirmation for Dedicated, and plan for model upgrades and evals. Action items agreed: share updated billing report, schedule benchmark for v2.1 model, and deliver SOC2 audit pack.
topics: Next steps: benchmarks, pricing, audit docs

SE to run 1-hour benchmark on v2.1 model with Acme test prompts (Liam) schedule week of 2025-02-24
Send SOC 2 in-scope docs and KMS integration guide (Maya) by 2025-02-18
Follow-up call to review benchmark and pricing adjustments (all) scheduled for 2025-03-03

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-12
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Nguyen (Redwood SE), Sofia Martinez (Acme - Head of ML), Rajesh Kumar (Acme - Platform), Lena Cho (Acme - Product), Tom Becker (Acme - Procurement)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is the QBR / health check for Acme — quick agenda, usage & cost, reliability incidents, roadmap alignment, and next steps. Sofia, do you want to kick off with any high level context?

[00:18] Sofia: Yeah thanks Maya. Overall thing is healthy, chat feature is in prod for three months now. Usage has ramped — about 600k tokens a day average, spikes 1.2M during promos. We're seeing costs creep up and want to understand where the spend is coming from. Also had a few user complaints about slow replies last month around the promo spike.

[00:40] Liam: Got it. We'll walk through the telemetry and then dig into the incidents. Quick note — are you still on the Dedicated cluster with 4xA100s?

[00:52] Rajesh: Correct, Dedicated pool, pinned model is rwd-v2.0-8b-quant (we're using 8-bit quant). We have autoscale but we capped burst due to budget.

[01:10] Lena: For product, we need predictability — latency under 600ms p95. On some days we're hitting around 1.4s p95 during spikes. That's not acceptable for live chat.

[01:30] Maya: Thanks, good callouts. On costs, preliminary glance shows embeddings and background vectorization jobs are a non-trivial chunk too. We'll send the detailed usage CSV after this call.

[01:45] Tom: From procurement, we need clarity on committed vs burst pricing. If we increase reserved capacity, what's the delta? Also need to understand minimum commitment.

[02:05] Liam: I'll cover the reliability bits — we have traces. The slowdowns look CPU and queueing related at the front end of the serving mesh during the 6pm promotion window. Two things: batch sizing went up during the spike which increased tail latency, and KV cache warmup was cold for several new sessions.

[02:32] Sofia: Can you explain the KV cache warmup? We thought cache was per model and persisted.

[02:40] Liam: Sure — with your workload we have prefix caching for common system prompts, but session-level cache is ephemeral on Dedicated unless you opt into longer-lived cache or shard affinity. During the spike many new sessions came in, cache misses were higher, resulting in extra decoder work. We can propose a cache policy change.

[03:05] Rajesh: Is that a config change or do we need infra changes?

[03:12] Liam: Mostly config — increase per-session cache TTL and enable prefix persistence for the route. There are tradeoffs in memory usage and cost.

[03:25] Maya: That ties back to cost; we can model out additional memory and justify it against token costs from re-generation. We'll include that in the billing breakdown.

[03:40] Sofia: On reliability, we also saw a short incident where one of the worker nodes had a GPU OOM and restarted, causing a 7-minute 5xx spike. How are you handling node restarts?

[03:54] Liam: Node restarts are expected but we have fast fallback — requests are routed to warm nodes; however you had limited warm capacity because autoscale was limited. We saw a small window where routing hit newly started nodes which delayed responses. Longer warm pools or faster pre-warming reduces that window.

[04:20] Lena: Would enabling burst capacity eliminate the issue? What's the cost tradeoff?

[04:28] Maya: Enabling burst reduces incident risk but increases cost during bursts; we can show modeled cost for one or two promotional events per month vs current spend.

[04:40] Tom: Procurement question: If we commit to higher reserved capacity, can we also get a cap on burst pricing or priority?

[04:50] Maya: Yes, with a reserved commitment we can provide better burst rates and priority in scheduling — terms to be included in the contract. We'll propose two tiers in the pricing doc.

[05:10] Sofia: Roadmap question — when will Redwood support the v2.1 model? We saw mention in the docs but want to know about quality/regression testing and rollout plan.

[05:22] Liam: v2.1 is in staging. We recommend running your eval set; we'll help run benchmarks for latency and quality. Typical rollout is canary on Dedicated, parallel evaluation, and then gradual shift. We'll run a 50k token/hour steady and spike test to match your promos.

[05:45] Rajesh: Can the canary be pinned to a subset of users? We want safe rollouts.

[05:52] Liam: Yes — routing policies let you split by route, region, or header. Canary with auto fallback to v2.0 if latency or quality regresses is straightforward to configure.

[06:06] Sofia: On security, procurement needs SOC2 docs and confirmation of KMS support for key management, and whether logs include PII or masked data by default.

[06:20] Maya: We'll send the SOC2 in-scope docs and KMS integration guide. Logs are editable; by default transcript logging includes tokens but we can mask or redact at ingestion. We also support customer-managed keys — HSM options available.

[06:38] Tom: Any caveats on compliance for EU data residency? We have some EU customers.

[06:45] Maya: Redwood Private supports VPC/on-prem; for hosted we have region controls and can route EU traffic to EU regions. We'll note options and possible data residency add-ons.

[06:58] Lena: For cost optimization — what are recommended levers? Quantization, batching, prefix caching?

[07:06] Liam: Right. Primary levers: quantization profile (you're on 8-bit, we can test 4-bit profiles if model supports it), intelligent batching (continuous batching tuned per latency SLO), and prefix/KV caching. Also consider async embeddings for background jobs instead of synchronous in-path calls.

[07:30] Sofia: We're worried 4-bit may degrade quality. Can we run A/B on prompts?

[07:36] Liam: Absolutely — we can run quality regressions using your eval sets. We'll include the eval harness results in the benchmark.

[07:50] Maya: For next steps, we'll send a detailed cost breakdown and proposed reserved commit options. SE will run the v2.1 benchmark with your prompts. We'll also provide SOC2 docs and KMS guide.

[08:05] Rajesh: Can we get an end-to-end runbook for incident response? The team would like a short runbook with steps and contacts.

[08:12] Maya: Yes — we'll provide a 1-page runbook plus escalation contacts.
notes: Customer currently on Redwood Dedicated, rwd-v2.0-8b-quant
Primary concerns: tail latency during spikes, cost growth, and SOC2/KMS documentation
Agreed to benchmarking v2.1 and provide cost modeling for reserved vs burst capacity
